proof_spans.independent_reasoning: The source uses a nonempty finite simple properly colored graph and surjective palette, with correlations permuting color classes. This is not an arbitrary uncolored automorphism definition. Geometry means every clique extends to a chamber; no unstated flag-transitivity or residual-connectedness hypothesis is introduced.

proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: Injectivity of the retained-copy map gives uniqueness of restriction and its multiplicativity from actual vertex actions. Pointwise rigidity kills exactly the restriction kernel. Existence of actual extensions proves surjectivity. The compatibility condition and surjectivity give equality, not merely containment, of the distinguished subgroups. None of homomorphic restriction, trivial kernel, or surjectivity is smuggled into its conclusion.

proof_spans.independent_reasoning: An element fixing S pointwise preserves each component boundary; distinct boundaries fix the components setwise. proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: Every clique involving a new vertex lies in its edge chamber; triangle-freeness leaves only old edges or singletons, and the empty clique also extends. New degrees are r−1 and old degrees d(v)(r−1)>r−1, recognizing the old graph. The old palette occurs in full, so an old-pointwise fixer fixes colors, and each new (edge,color) vertex is unique. The explicit extension and its inverse preserve adjacency and the pair. r=2 adds no vertices and is included. The source degree arithmetic is corrected without weakening its actual minimum-degree hypothesis.

proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: Nonemptiness gives M>=1 and q>=1. The two fresh classes have distinct sizes q(M+3),q(M+2), both larger than M, and recognize the old vertex set. Two old vertices have a common fresh neighbor exactly for an old edge. Each deleted-old component has its own singleton or edge boundary. For an isolated old vertex, its attached u0 and u2 have different total degrees; after root recognition, tail branches are distinguished by degrees INSIDE the gadget. This also handles M=1, where the isolated attachment changes a total degree but not the internal degree comparison. Index-preserving extensions provide the inverse restriction. Minimum degree, triangle-freeness, component preservation and the added-vertex count are all separately justified.

proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: The quantifier is a finite normal subgroup H of G. Connectedness follows from the explicit encoder, not from cleaning arbitrary input. The nontrivial construction has rank [G:H]+3, while G=1 has a one-vertex rank-one geometry. There is no universal rank-two statement.

proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: Old vertices have degree 4(q−1)>=4; all gadget vertices have degree at most three. Among the degree-two neighbors T_xy of P_x, the unique one at distance two from P_y identifies the ordered arrow. Its other neighbor is the degree-three terminal, whose intrinsic path through degree-two interiors has length k+2>=4 and ends at the degree-three initial vertex. The other terminal-to-initial route passes through old vertices of degree at least four, so it cannot be confused. This proves full UNCOLORED rigidity and label recovery. Label preservation forces rho(y)rho(x)^−1=yx^−1 and hence right translation. The inverse in P_x↦P_xg^−1 fixes ordinary-composition convention. Normality makes right translation permute right-coset colors; the exact kernel is H. Triangle-freeness, connectedness, counts and minimum degree are proved explicitly, including q=2.

proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: The n=2 path gives (S2,1) but has leaves. Even representatives g_j mapping n to j exist for n>=3 and make the local permutation g_sigma(j)^−1 sigma g_j have the same parity as sigma. Boundary labels agree in overlapping copies and the displayed cocycle proves a genuine S_n action. The color-size recurrence proves the formula. The top class is uniquely smallest for n>=4; at n=3 degree-neighbor signatures recognize it. The missing faithfulness detail is fully paid: X_m minus its top row is connected by induction, and deleting the top and pair rows of X_n leaves exactly the interiors of attached copies with distinct boundary stars. This recognizes each copy for a top fixer and allows induction. Minimum degree two begins at n=3; n=2 is cleaned before completion. No blanket identification with (Aut(A_n),Inn(A_n)) is used.

proof_spans.scope: Complete named statement/proof or declared context; overlapping locators are not cost partitions
proof_spans.independent_reasoning: The old base hexagon is recognized by degree, so the initial three-tip graph gives the stabilizer of an alternating edge set: correlation S3 and palette kernel C3. With all six tips, all dihedral symmetries extend; even rotations and reflections i↦2a−i form the color-preserving S3. The explicit reflection i↦−i, tip_i↦tip_(−i−1) has order two and already contradicts the printed C3 kernel. The resulting full pair is (D12,S3), where 12 is the group order. The initial graph already has triangles, so this example is not a proof of optimality of every completion hypothesis.
